start.text: Out past the legs the fog stands up like a wall. At the foot of it, on a tussock no bigger than a table, a man is standing.

A big man, in a fisher's knit gone grey with wet. A lantern hangs from his hand. It isn't lit. He is looking down into the water the way the others do, but he's standing up to do it, the way a man stands on a boat.
Your ember's light doesn't reach him. He hasn't seen it.

called.text: Your voice goes out flat across the water and the fog takes the end of it.
He stops. His head comes up. He doesn't turn.
After a while he steps down off the tussock into the grey, as easily as off a quay, and the dark lantern goes with him, and he's gone.

nameless.text: You open your mouth to call him, and there's no name in it. You know there was one. Mara said it; Oda said it. It goes past you like rain off a coat.
By the time you've stopped reaching for it, he has stepped down off the tussock into the grey, and the dark lantern with him.

watched.text: You watch. He stands a long while, looking into the water.
Then he steps down off the tussock into the grey as if into a room he knows, and the dark lantern swings once, and he's gone.

cord.text: As he goes, something at his belt flicks red. A bit of cord.
Nobody follows them with a light. That's the rule out here.
